title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of type 1 diabetes.

HPI
The patient presents today for a routine follow-up regarding their type 1 diabetes mellitus. The patient reports that they have been experiencing symptoms of hyperglycemia over the past two weeks, including increased thirst and frequent urination. They continue to manage their condition with long-term insulin therapy and do not take any oral medications for their condition. The patient notes that their blood glucose levels have been poorly controlled despite consistent adherence to their current regimen.

Medication List
- Insulin (long-term)

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented. Physical examination reveals clear breath sounds and normal heart rate. Skin is intact with no signs of infection or acute distress.

Assessment
1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus.
2. Hyperglycemia.

Plan
We will continue the current insulin regimen. The patient was instructed to monitor blood glucose levels more frequently and keep a log for review at the next appointment. We will discuss further adjustments to the insulin dosage if the hyperglycemia persists. Follow up in four weeks.
explanations: Type 1 diabetes with hyperglycemia / poor control: E10.65.
Do not assign Z79.4 for type 1 diabetes; insulin use is inherent.

distractors.why: Z79.4 is not assigned for type 1 diabetes.
